newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers deny funds for pension scheme office.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers deny funds for pension scheme office.

text.p: A subcommittee of Hong Kong's Legislative Council (Legco) has voted to deny further funding to the office of the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF), a Legco spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

The establishment sub-committee of Legco's Finance Committee voted 11 to six to deny the MPF office HK$25 million (US$3.2 million) that would have kept the office operational for the 13 months from March, allowing it to complete its work.
Hong Kong's proposed Mandatory Provident Fund would require individual employees and employers to each contribute five percent of a monthly salary to a retirement fund.
The MPF office is charged with recommending guidelines to balance the risks and returns of MPF investments.
Some legislators have opposed the MPF, fearing that workers' assets would be at risk because the funds would be managed by the private sector rather than by the Hong Kong government.
The opponents instead favour a government-managed system similar to Singapore's Centralised Provident Fund.
Members of Hong Kong's Democratic Party were joined by representatives from the territory's pro-China grassroots parties in opposing the new funding.
Committee members voting in favor of extending the MPF office's mandate were largely from pro-business sectors.
Pamela Tan, director of the MPF office, said "we regret the decision very much because we feel that the MPF is something that is good for Hong Kong."
Tan said the next step for the MPF office is to submit a funding proposal to the full Finance Committee before the office's money runs out at the end of February.
If that submission were to fail, "then the office would have to shut down and we would not have a dedicated office to look after the MPF," said Tan.
She said no date has been set as yet for the new submission.
